title: Yellow Card CEO on Funding, Stablecoin’s Global Foothold
title_cn: 黄牌首席执行官谈资金、稳定币的全球立足点
summary: Chris Maurice, CEO of Yellow Card, explained how his company differentiates itself from competitors like Stripe and Wise by building the underlying infrastructure that enables international money movement using stablecoins such as USDC. Yellow Card provides direct liquidity and on/off ramps against local currencies across regions including Africa, Latin America, and Asia, allowing stablecoins to be sent and converted locally without the need to convert back to dollars first. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

summary: During the countdown to the market close, Romaine Bostick highlighted the recent surge in private debt defaults, noting that Fitch Ratings reported a record 6% default rate among 1,300 US private debt borrowers in the second quarter. Randy Schwimmer, Vice Chairman and Chief Investment Strategist at Churchill Asset Management, acknowledged the challenging environment reflected in the rising defaults but expressed optimism about improving conditions in the second half of the year. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

(Source: Bloomberg)

title: OpenAI Hack Could Have Been 'Way Worse,' Hugging Face CEO Says

summary: Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue says a hack by OpenAI could have been "way worse" if not for the company's defensive measures. He calls this a "wake up call" for the industry and says the incident has been reported to lawmakers and authorities. He speaks to Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow on "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: 'Concentration of Power' One of Biggest Risks in AI, Says Hugging Face CEO
title_cn: Hugging Face 首席执行官表示，“权力集中”是人工智能最大的风险之一
summary: Clement Delangue, CEO of AI company Hugging Face,  sat down with Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow to discuss OpenAI models' hack on Hugging Face last month and the future of AI regulation. Talking about the hack, Delangue, said that while companies want AI agents to think outside the box, they don't want AI to 'think outside the sandbox' and stay in the closed testing environment. Delangue also discussed government involvement in AI regulation and said that there is a risk that too much government intervention would result in a 'concentration of power' and said that is one of the biggest risks in the AI space.  (Source: Bloomberg)

On today's show, Ambassador James Jeffrey, Distinguished Fellow at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy and former US Ambassador to Iraq and Turkey, discusses ongoing negotiations between the US and Iran, focusing on President Trump's repeated ultimatums and threats of escalation. Robert McWhirter, founder of the Law Office of Robert McWhirter, says acting attorney general Todd Blanche’s written pledge to terminate the administration’s $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund is legally unenforceable, arguing that “a pinky swear has far more force.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Blanche Strikes Deal With Holdouts to Advance His Nomination
title_cn: 布兰奇与坚持不懈的人达成协议以推进他的提名
summary: Holdout Republican senators are backing a deal with acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to formally rescind an order creating an “anti-weaponization fund” that could have paid $1.8 billion to President Donald Trump’s allies, likely clearing the way for Blanche’s confirmation as the nation’s top law enforcement officer.

title: Treasury Sued Over Lawsuit Settlement Payouts to Trump Allies
title_cn: 财政部因向特朗普盟友支付诉讼和解金而被起诉
summary: The US Treasury Department was sued by a nonprofit group claiming the government is improperly withholding legal settlements that the Trump administration could use to cover payouts to pardoned Jan. 6 defendants and other supporters of the president.

title: Trump: Latest Talks 'Last Chance' for Iran | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/3/2026
title_cn: 特朗普：最新会谈对伊朗来说是“最后的机会”彭博商业周刊日报 8/3/2026
summary: President Trump says talks are happening with Iran, and that he wants to give the country a last chance before "decapitation." Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason reacts to the President's latest comments on Iran, plus the announcement from Acting AG Todd Blanche that the DOJ is rescinding the anti-weaponization fund order. Then, Torsten Slok, Chief Economist at Apollo, says the economic impacts from the war in Iran remains one of the most important factors as the Fed continues to weight interest rate hikes. Finally, Goldman Sachs Senior Equity Research Analyst Lizzie Dove talks Marriott earnings, and the war's impact on the travel and leisure sector. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump’s Latest Tariffs Hit With New Lawsuit by 25 States
title_cn: 特朗普的最新关税遭到 25 个州的新诉讼
summary: A group of 25 US states filed a lawsuit challenging President Donald Trump’s new global tariffs that went into effect last month, adding to similar complaints by groups of small businesses who claim the levies are illegal.

title: Israel’s Strikes on Gaza Cast Doubt on Peace Plan Revival
title_cn: 以色列对加沙的袭击使和平计划复兴受到质疑
summary: Israel has stepped up strikes in Gaza since Hamas conditionally agreed to disarm late last week, sparking concerns that President Donald Trump’s proclaimed revival in a long-delayed peace plan may have been premature.

title: Blanche Deal Could Face Pitfalls as Senate Clock Ticks Down
title_cn: 随着参议院时钟的流逝，布兰奇协议可能面临陷阱
summary: GOP holdouts backed Trump’s pick for attorney general but pitfalls remain
